# desktop

```go
import "github.com/shdeen/saferm/cmd/saferm-app/desktop"
```

Package desktop connects the GUI and SafeRM Notify to the operating system: handing a launch to a running instance, registering SafeRM Notify to start at login, opening the GUI for a review, and logging errors.

<a name="ForwardActivation"></a>
## func ForwardActivation

```go
func ForwardActivation(_ string) (bool, error)
```

ForwardActivation forwards nothing and reports false. On macOS and Linux, Wails hands a launch to the running instance by itself.

<a name="LogError"></a>
## func LogError

```go
func LogError(operationErr error)
```

LogError appends the error, with a timestamp and the process ID, to notifications.log in the SafeRM directory. A nil error writes nothing. When the log cannot be written, the error goes to the standard logger instead.

<a name="Review"></a>
## func Review

```go
func Review(actionID int64) error
```

Review starts the GUI executable that is packaged with the running SafeRM Notify, passing \-\-review and the action ID. It returns ErrInputInvalid for a nonpositive ID.

<a name="Setup"></a>
## func Setup

```go
func Setup(home, guiExecutable string) error
```

Setup registers the SafeRM Notify executable that is packaged with the GUI executable to start at login, then writes a marker file in the SafeRM directory. Setup does nothing when the marker exists, so a user who later disables SafeRM Notify stays unregistered. It also does nothing when SafeRM Notify is not packaged.

<a name="notifierExecutablePath"></a>
## func notifierExecutablePath

```go
func notifierExecutablePath(guiExecutable string) string
```

notifierExecutablePath returns the location where this operating system's package places the SafeRM Notify executable, given the GUI executable's path.

<a name="registerNotifier"></a>
## func registerNotifier

```go
func registerNotifier(notifierPath string) error
```

registerNotifier registers SafeRM Notify as a login item through saferm\_register\_notifier. On failure, it returns ErrNotifierSetup with the system's description of the failure.

<a name="waitProcess"></a>
## func waitProcess

```go
func waitProcess(command *exec.Cmd)
```

waitProcess waits for the started process to exit and logs its failure.
